newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ should further reform electricity industry -IEA.
newsitem.headline: NZ should further reform electricity industry -IEA.

text.p: The government should consider a further split of Electricity Corp of New Zealand (ECNZ) and privatisation of the two state-owned generators, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Monday.
Paris-based IEA, set up under the auspices of the OECD, said potential for competition in generation was limited by the large market share held by ECNZ and Contact Energy.
It said in its four-yearly report the government and industry would have to monitor pricing closely to identify whether the generators were abusing their dominant market position.
"The government should consider the merits of a further break-up of ECNZ's generation business," it said.

"The ownership of ECNZ and Contact Energy may also need to be addressed given question marks over whether the two companies can compete fairly with private companies for the opportunity to build new plant."
Contract Energy was established in April last year as the junior competitor for ECNZ.
The government has so far ruled out privatisation of the state-owned enterprises, but has allowed the sale of some power stations.

The IEA also questioned the effectiveness of the existing regulatory regime in preventing monopoly abuse in distribution and retailing and suggested a more rigorous regulatory approach may be needed for the gas sector.
The IEA review team came to New Zealand last September for its review, speaking with government officials and industry representatives.
Energy Minister Max Bradford there may be a case for a further breakup of ECNZ.
"I and other ministers are giving some consideration to that at the present time," Bradford told a news conference.
Bradford said privatisation of either state generating companies was "not on the agenda of reform in the life of this government".
However, while no formal policy work had been carried out, further breaking up of ECNZ was being discussed, he said, and the issue would need to be addressed later this year.
